transcript.content: Hello, I'm Dr. Smith, welcome in. What brings you in to see me today?

Hi, Dr. Smith. Um… I guess what brought me in is I’ve been having a harder time staying on one thing. It’s not terrible, I don’t think, but over the past year or so, little stuff—like my phone buzzing, someone walking past my office, or even some random thought popping in—can pull me off what I’m doing before I really catch myself. I figured it might be worth asking about, if that makes sense.
Thinking back, did you notice similar problems with staying focused when you were a kid or teenager, or is this really a new pattern that started within the last year or so?

Yeah… I mean, I don’t want to make it sound like I was some awful kid or anything, but looking back, it probably was there then too. Teachers would move my seat sometimes because I was talking too much, or I’d get up when I wasn’t supposed to, or I’d answer before they even finished asking the question. I guess I always thought of it as just being energetic or impatient, but yeah, it wasn’t only something that started this past year.
When your attention drifts like that, do you notice you're often preoccupied with worry or anxious thoughts, or does your mind just wander to random things without a specific worry attached?

Most of the time it’s not worry, no. I mean, I can worry like anyone, but when this happens it’s usually just… something pulls me. Like my phone buzzes, or someone walks past my office, and suddenly I’m off track. Or even some random thought, like something about my in-laws, pops in and I’m following that before I realize it. It’s not usually some big anxious spiral, if that answers it right.
Would you say these issues with focus and impulsivity cause noticeable problems both at work and in your home or personal life?

Yeah… I mean, I’m still keeping up overall, so I don’t want to overstate it. But yes, it’s starting to show up in both places.

At work, people are pretty patient with me, but I can tell in meetings or mentoring conversations, if I jump ahead or get pulled off track, it wears on them a bit. And at home, it’s more like… family plans don’t always go the way they should, or my wife feels like she can’t fully count on me to stay with what we agreed on. I don’t love saying that, but yeah, it’s starting to cost me some trust there.

final_diagnosis.reason: The patient reports chronic, longstanding difficulties with sustained attention, distractibility by external stimuli and intrusive thoughts, and impulsivity (interrupting, blurting answers, difficulty staying seated) beginning in childhood and persisting into adulthood. These symptoms are not primarily driven by anxious rumination, arguing against a primary anxiety disorder.
